audit.whatIsWrong: "Dash Chain" is a fabricated ability name and it is the spine of this entire page — focus.text, tldr, winCon, enemyWin, tradeBad, loading, breakdown.cooldowns, three dos/donts and four report rows all key off it. Ambessa has no ability by that name.
audit.why: Riot gives her Drakehound's Step (P, the dash woven into every cast), Cunning Sweep / Sundering Slam (Q, 14s at rank 1), Repudiation (W, 18s, shield then slam, grounding), Lacerate (E, 13s, dash + slow) and Public Execution (R, 130s, blinks to the FARTHEST enemy champion in her chosen line, suppresses, then stuns).
audit.corrected: The dash-weaving references now say Drakehound's Step; the lockdown references that describe a lane-ending commit now say Public Execution, which is the ability that actually does it. Real cooldowns added — Lacerate 13s is the tell to step up on.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart was shifted a stage out of alignment with its own why text — the mirror recorded the same defect from Ambessa's side.
audit.why: whys[0] 'you're both weak' = Skill, whys[1] 'Ambessa owns the level 2 spike', whys[2] 'at 3 you finally layer Q sweetspot' = Lillia, whys[3] 'her peak', whys[4] 'her combo out-trades you here', whys[5] 'you can finally bite back', whys[6] 'you pick skirmishes'. That is exactly the packet chart, and none of the seven stored rows matched it.
audit.corrected: All seven rows flipped in matched full/content pairs to Skill/Ambessa/Lillia/Ambessa/Ambessa/Lillia/Lillia with ratings 5/3/7/3/3/7/7, and all seven full-layer why lines rewritten (they were boilerplate about a treadmill lane that does not exist here).

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer put your spikes at Level 6 and hers at first item; it is the reverse.
audit.why: Level 6 is HER spike — Public Execution blinks to the farthest champion in the line, suppresses and stuns, and a suppression on a champion with no dash and no shield ends the fight. Your spike is Liandry's, where the DoT starts paying percent HP.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now states Public Execution's farthest-target blink and the suppression; phases[5].why states your item turn.
